title.en: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

text.en: Rani notices that she is taller, her voice and moods are changing and she wants more privacy. These changes are a normal part of growing up called adolescence.

Adolescence is the stage from about 10 to 19 years when a child grows into an adult. Many adolescents grow taller and notice changes in their body shape, skin, hair or voice. Some begin having menstrual periods. The timing and extent of these changes can differ from person to person. These changes happen at different times for different people and are completely normal.
Hormones are chemical signals made in our bodies. Certain hormones help coordinate changes during puberty, along with other processes such as growth. The pituitary gland sits at the base of the brain. It releases hormones that help regulate growth and send signals to some other glands.
Eat a balanced diet with enough iron and calcium, sleep well, exercise and keep the body clean. Keeping the body and clothes clean and caring for teeth are everyday hygiene habits. During a period, access to clean menstrual products, a private place to change and a place to wash hands supports hygiene.
Mood swings, anger and worry are common in adolescence. Talking to parents, teachers or a trusted adult helps. Choose friends wisely and avoid harmful habits such as tobacco.

Place childhood, adolescence and adulthood on a timeline. The boundaries are approximate because real people develop at different rates.
Puberty is the name for a set of physical changes that happens during adolescence. Adolescence also includes changes in feelings, interests, friendships and choices.
Compare fictional height records for two students. One grows quickly earlier in the timeline and the other grows quickly later. Each record tells a story about that student’s own growth.

board.text: Growth spurts can start at different times

text.en: Comparing progress over time tells us more than ranking classmates by height. We can use fictional examples to learn the science and let other people keep their personal measurements private.
The voice box, also called the larynx, helps make sound. As it grows, a voice can change pitch and may crack from time to time. The amount of change varies.

board.text: Growth of the voice box can affect pitch

text.en: Body hair and changes in the skin can become more noticeable around puberty. Acne can include pimples. These changes vary, and an observation about someone’s skin is not a reason to tease them.

board.text: Skin and hair can change at different rates

text.en: In the hormonal signals diagram, follow an arrow from one part of the body to another. Organs that receive a signal can respond. Different hormones have different roles.
Some signals help coordinate reproductive development. This process is gradual and can happen alongside changes in height, voice and body shape.
Menstruation is the shedding of some of the lining inside the uterus. During a period, blood and tissue leave the body. It is a natural process that can begin during puberty.

board.text: Menstrual period: part of a cycle

text.en: People can start their first period at different times. Even for the same person, the time between periods can vary. A typical age or interval in a textbook is a guide to the idea of variation.

board.text: Starting ages and cycles can vary

text.en: Imagine a student needs a menstrual product at school. A private place to change, handwashing facilities and knowing which adult can help make the school day easier.

Growing bodies use energy and nutrients from a variety of foods. In a food chart, beans, vegetables, grains and other foods can help illustrate that a balanced pattern draws from different food groups.

board.text: Draw from a variety of food groups

text.en: Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, the substance in red blood cells that carries oxygen. This gives us one example of how nutrients support the body as it grows.
A daily routine can make room for sleep, physical activity and things you enjoy. Compare two fictional timetables and notice where each leaves time for movement and rest.

board.text: Find time for rest and activity

text.en: A body change and a feeling are different things to observe. A student might notice a new interest, want more privacy or feel upset after a disagreement. Friends can respond with respect and listen.
Suppose an upsetting message arrives in a group chat. A student can pause before replying, talk to a trusted adult and ask for help if the messages continue.
A friend asks for another student’s photo or personal details. Ask permission before sharing a person’s information. Everyone has a right to decide what they keep private.
Imagine a friend offers tobacco or asks you to try alcohol. Practise a simple response: no, I do not want to. Then think of a trusted adult you could talk to if you feel pressured.
Interest in a hobby or an idea can grow during adolescence too. Clubs, sports, art and helpful work at home or school can give us ways to explore new interests and make friends.

board.text: Explore new interests and ways to take part

text.en: Sometimes a worry keeps returning or gets in the way of school. A parent, teacher or another trusted adult can listen and help you work out what support you need.

board.text: Talk to a trusted adult when a worry persists

text.en: Use a fictional example to wrap up. Identify one sign of physical development, one change in feelings or behaviour and one practical way you could support the person respectfully.

problem.en: What role does iron have in red blood cells?

text.en: Haemoglobin is part of a red blood cell.

why.en: It carries oxygen around the body.

text.en: Iron is part of haemoglobin.

why.en: A nutrient can contribute to a specific job the body needs to do.

prompt.en: How could you support a friend who has a worry they would like to share?

requiredIdeas.en: Help them identify a trusted adult if they want support.

commonMisconceptions.en: Everyone of the same age experiences changes in the same way.

points.en: Adolescence is a stage of growth from about 10 to 19.
Hygiene and good food are needed.
